artifacts.summary: 8-phase plan adding the hold task status: enum + schema twin + field allowlist (standalone Phase 1), dispatch exclusion, operator-settable/reversible hold, /todo audit, documentation, 13-value prose sweep, and live consumer-repo acceptance.

memory_candidates.content: When adding a status value whose semantics are a THIRD category relative to an existing binary split, the mechanical cost is concentrated in every two-arm `case` statement that encodes the old binary. In this codebase that pattern recurs as `case "$status" in completed|abandoned|expanded) ... ;; *) ... ;; esac` and appears in orchestrate STAGE 0, command-gate-in.sh, generate-todo.sh's count split, and the /todo subtask-blocking check -- the last of which is near-byte-duplicated between skills/skill-todo/SKILL.md and commands/todo.md, so any decision must be applied to both or they silently diverge. Plan such a feature by enumerating the two-arm case sites first (grep the shared pattern, not the feature name), deciding per site whether the new value joins an existing arm or needs its own, and recording a 'leave unmodified' decision explicitly where no change is correct -- an unrecorded non-change is indistinguishable from an oversight. Separately: a closed enum's size asserted in PROSE comments spreads far beyond the enum's own file (11 files here), including disambiguating cross-references in unrelated scripts; sweep by grepping the number, not the enum name.
